packages.title: Road freight 2025 tonnes lifted QA
facts: DfT reports 1.53 billion tonnes of goods lifted by GB-registered HGVs operating in the UK in 2025.
Tonnes lifted measures freight activity.
It is not tonnes of CO2e.
GB-registered vehicle scope must be preserved.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Road freight tonne-km versus vehicle-km QA
facts: DfT reports 162 billion tonne-kilometres and 19.0 billion vehicle-kilometres for GB-registered HGV activity in 2025.
Tonne-km combines goods mass and distance.
Vehicle-km measures vehicle movement.
Neither metric is a greenhouse-gas quantity without an emissions method.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Road freight GB-registered scope QA
facts: Domestic road-freight statistics focus on GB-registered HGVs operating in the UK.
Foreign-registered HGVs are excluded from the cited domestic statistics.
Vehicles at or below 3.5 tonnes are also excluded.
Fleet-scope exclusions must be retained.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Road freight sample-estimate QA
facts: The road-freight survey uses a stratified sample of HGVs.
DfT weights sampled vehicles to represent the HGV population.
The 2025 GB-registered sample contained 8,346 vehicles.
Survey estimates have potential sampling error.
No sample result is treated as direct parcel measurement.

packages.title: Road traffic 2025 vehicle-miles QA
facts: DfT reports 2025 Great Britain traffic in vehicle miles by vehicle type.
Car traffic was 262.4 billion vehicle miles and van traffic 58.8 billion vehicle miles.
Lorry traffic was 16.3 billion vehicle miles.
Vehicle miles are activity rather than CO2e.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Road traffic mode-trend QA
facts: DfT reports different 2025 changes for cars, vans and lorries relative to 2024 and 2019.
Vehicle classes must remain separate in trend comparisons.
Traffic growth does not imply the same percentage change in emissions.
Fleet efficiency and fuel type are separate factors.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Road length 2025 versus traffic QA
facts: DfT estimates 247,200 miles of publicly maintained road in Great Britain in 2025.
Road length is infrastructure stock.
It is not vehicle traffic, fuel use or GHG emissions.
Major and minor road length categories must remain distinct.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Bus fares January-March 2026 QA
facts: DfT published quarterly bus fares statistics for January to March 2026 on 18 June 2026.
Bus fares are price statistics.
Fare indices are not passenger counts or emissions.
Quarterly reference periods must be retained.
No parcel GHG value is inferred.

packages.title: Bus operator survey scope QA
facts: Most annual bus statistics are sourced from a survey of more than 500 bus operators.
Other bus statistics use local-authority or large-operator sources.
Survey-source differences must be preserved.
Bus activity metrics do not directly measure CO2e.
No parcel inference is made.

packages.title: Bus revised-tables QA
facts: DfT records revisions to bus tables including BUS01 and BUS02_mi.
Revision metadata must accompany extracted historical values.
A revised table can supersede an earlier published value.
Revision status is separate from emissions meaning.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: CAA Q1-2026 passenger-volume QA
facts: The UK Civil Aviation Authority reports more than 61 million passengers through UK airports in Q1 2026.
CAA states Q1 2026 was a record first quarter for passenger numbers.
Passenger counts are aviation activity metrics.
They are not aviation GHG emissions.
No airport parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: CAA passengers versus emissions QA
facts: CAA passenger trends describe demand and airport throughput.
Passenger growth does not directly quantify fuel burn or CO2e.
Route length, aircraft type and load factors are separate determinants.
Activity and emissions datasets must remain distinct.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: 2026 conversion factors require activity data QA
facts: DESNZ 2026 conversion factors calculate GHG emissions from activity data such as fuel volume, electricity kWh or distance.
A conversion factor alone is not an emissions observation.
Activity quantity and matching factor are both required.
Factor scope and year must be preserved.
No parcel emissions are inferred without parcel activity data.

packages.title: 2026 conversion factors Scope 1-2-3 QA
facts: DESNZ states the reporting factors support separate Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 reporting.
Scope categories must not be merged without an explicit reporting boundary.
Purchased electricity and direct fuel combustion have different scopes.
Corporate reporting factors do not establish parcel geometry.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: REPD April-2026 project-status QA
facts: DESNZ published the April 2026 Renewable Energy Planning Database extract on 6 May 2026.
REPD monitors renewable-energy projects and planning/development status.
A project record can represent planning or operational stages.
Project status is not electricity generation or GHG output.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: REPD capacity versus generation QA
facts: REPD project records include capacity-related project information.
Installed or planned capacity is not generated electricity.
Generation depends on operation and capacity factors.
Generation itself is still not direct parcel GHG without a method.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: REPD planning versus operational QA
facts: REPD includes projects at multiple planning and development stages.
A planning application does not prove a project is constructed or operating.
Planning dates and operational dates must remain separate.
Future capacity must not be treated as current generation.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Smart-meter Q1-2026 installation QA
facts: DESNZ reports 590,000 smart and advanced meters installed by large suppliers in Great Britain in Q1 2026.
Quarterly installations are flow data.
Installations are not energy consumption.
Supplier coverage and quarter must be preserved.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Smart-meter operating versus installed QA
facts: At end March 2026 DESNZ reports over 41 million smart and advanced meters in homes and small businesses across Great Britain.
Over 38 million were operating in smart mode or classified as advanced meters.
Installed stock and operating-smart stock are distinct metrics.
Meter status does not report kWh or emissions.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Smart-meter Great Britain scope QA
facts: The smart-meter quarterly release applies to England, Scotland and Wales.
That is Great Britain rather than the full United Kingdom.
GB coverage must not be relabelled UK coverage.
Meter counts do not measure emissions.
No parcel GHG value is inferred.

packages.title: Ofgem BUS application-issued-redeemed QA
facts: Ofgem's June-2026 BUS update reports voucher applications, vouchers issued and vouchers redeemed separately.
These stages are not interchangeable.
Scheme activity does not directly measure installed-system heat output or CO2e savings.
Withdrawn, expired and rejected cases affect stage counts.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Ofgem BUS dynamic-budget QA
facts: Ofgem states the remaining Year-5 BUS budget is dynamic.
Undetermined applications and issued-but-unredeemed vouchers are included in the budget context.
Expired or returned vouchers can make budget available again.
Budget value is not an emissions metric.
No parcel GHG value is inferred.

packages.title: New-dwelling EPC modelled-characteristics QA
facts: MHCLG new-dwelling energy-efficiency statistics use lodged EPC data for England.
They estimate features such as heating systems, heat pumps and solar PV under Part L reporting.
The series is Official Statistics in Development.
EPC/design characteristics are not measured operational GHG emissions.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: Local-GHG model and uncertainty QA
facts: DESNZ local-authority GHG statistics are nationally consistent spatial estimates.
The technical report documents sector-specific disaggregation and uncertainty methods.
Local estimates combine administrative, inventory and modelled inputs.
Local-authority estimates are not direct parcel measurements.
No parcel value is inferred without verified geometry/source binding.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel-inference guard 104 QA
facts: Batch 104 combines official transport, fuel, ETS, infrastructure, energy and building sources.
The sources use different geographies, units, periods and accounting boundaries.
None of the reviewed sources supplies a verified parcel-level emissions measurement for this slot.
Cross-source synthesis preserves each source boundary and revision status.
Parcel binding remains false and no synthetic parcel value is produced.
